what_it_does: Running large AI language models efficiently often means storing the model's weights (its learned parameters) using a compressed number format — fewer bits per number — to save memory. A common strategy keeps the input data in full-precision floating-point (numbers with decimal places) while compressing the weights to small integers. The problem is that multiplying a floating-point number by an integer is awkward for standard hardware. FIGLUT sidesteps this by precomputing all possible multiplication results and storing them in a lookup table — essentially a cheat sheet — so that at inference time the hardware just looks up the answer instead of doing the multiply. The design supports different compression levels in a single fixed piece of hardware, making it flexible and energy-efficient.
